# Home Environment Manager v0.5.0 — Opt-in climate PID control

This release introduces an independent, opt-in, room-scoped supervisory PID
thermostat setpoint regulator, in addition to the international environmental
monitoring and scientifically grounded comfort/ventilation methods in v0.4.0.

## Safety-focused control

- **Default OFF for every new or existing room.** Climate devices are selected
  explicitly and the PID controller only writes `climate.set_temperature`
  to those entities. It never switches HVAC modes or turns compressors on/off.
- The controller's P, I and D terms are evaluated from fresh room temperature
  measurements. It has conditional anti-windup, derivative-on-measurement,
  bounded setpoint trim, sample cadence and maximum change per cycle.
- Only an existing compatible `heat` or `cool` single-setpoint climate mode
  is supported. Dual temperature-range climate modes are not controlled.
- Open or unknown windows, stale room measurements, active device presets,
  unsupported unit/range, conflicting device assignment and out-of-area
  selections stop setpoint commands.
- A manual thermostat setpoint/mode change or service error latches a pause
  that is persisted over restarts. The room must be explicitly resumed using
  its dashboard or `home_environment_manager.pid_control` action.
- Sensor/device failure does not make the controller toggle off, reset the
  HVAC mode or send a last guessed setpoint. Existing equipment protections
  remain indispensable.

## User interface and compatibility

- Configure one monitored room at a time under **Climate PID**, first picking
  thermostat and sensor, then optionally tuning Kp/Ki/Kd, bounds and cadence.
- The existing Lovelace room card shows PID effort, target, requested thermostat
  setpoint and pause/resume controls.
- The established `air_quality_advisor` integration domain and legacy sensor
  unique IDs remain untouched, as do the Announcement Hub room routing and
  previous v0.4 scientific monitoring and local histories.
- The new English/German/Greek PID form labels and all existing locale files
  are provided with English fallback for untranslated new technical concepts.

**This is supervisory thermostat setpoint control, not direct cycle-length PID
of a compressor or heater relay.** Do not use without independent device
overtemperature, freeze or compressor safety protections.

The HACS release is published only after Python/JS regression tests,
translations, Hassfest and HACS validation succeed.
